message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant traits is the **presence of a mane in males**. The gene that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion: a single copy of the dominant allele is enough for a male lion to grow a mane, while females (who are typically mane‑less) carry the recessive allele. This dominant trait is what gives male lions their iconic, shaggy head and neck fur.
